name: DRV8311HRRWR
title: DRV8311H / DRV8311S / DRV8311P: three-phase PWM motor driver with integrated MOSFETs, current sensing and 3.3 V LDO, 3 V to 20 V, 5 A peak, WQFN-24
summary: A three-phase brushless-DC motor driver holding three N-channel MOSFET half-bridges (210 mΩ typical, high plus low side), their gate drivers, a charge pump for the high-side gates, three low-side current sense amplifiers that need no shunt resistor, and a 3.3 V, 100 mA linear regulator for outside circuits. It runs from 3 V to 20 V (24 V absolute) and delivers 5 A peak. The H variant is set up by pins (MODE, SLEW, GAIN) and takes 6x or 3x PWM inputs; the S variant is set up over SPI and also offers internal PWM generation; the P variant uses tSPI, which lets several drivers share one chip select, and generates its PWM internally with duty and period written over the bus. Protection covers supply, charge-pump and regulator undervoltage, overcurrent and over-temperature, reported on an open-drain nFAULT pin.
key_figures: 3 V to 20 V recommended, 24 V absolute maximum
210 mΩ typ, 250 mΩ max (VVM ≥ 6 V, 1 A, TJ = 25 °C)
WQFN-24 (RRW), 3 mm × 3 mm, 0.4 mm pitch, exposed pad

circuits.title: Three-phase BLDC drive, DRV8311S with SPI and 6x PWM
circuits.description: A microcontroller drives the six PWM inputs directly and configures the driver over SPI. A buck regulator turns VM into the VIN_AVDD supply, and the 3.3 V AVDD output powers the controller, the optional Hall sensors and any other load. A voltage supervisor fed from that rail sets CSAREF, which the controller also reads on an ADC; the three SOx outputs go to three more ADC inputs for phase current. nFAULT is pulled up to the 3.3 V rail and read on a GPIO. The motor's three windings connect to OUTA, OUTB and OUTC.

parts.note: CAVDD; X5R or X7R, 6.3 V recommended
CSAREF bypass; X5R or X7R recommended

notes: The DRV8311S has no nSLEEP pin (pin 24 is nSCS); the nSLEEP connection applies to the H and P variants.
C7, C8 and R1 take the recommended external-component values.
The third Hall sensor should read C.
Ground pins of the controller, supervisor, buck regulator and Hall sensors are outside this circuit.

circuits.title: Three-phase BLDC drive, DRV8311P over tSPI
circuits.description: The DRV8311P generates its own PWM; the controller sets duty and period over tSPI and sends a PWM_SYNC reference from a GPIO. AD0 and AD1 give the device its address on a bus shared with other DRV8311P parts under one chip select. Power, current sensing, the CSAREF reference (in this circuit from a voltage regulator), nFAULT and the motor connect as in the SPI drive circuit.

parts.note: CAVDD; X5R or X7R, 6.3 V recommended
CSAREF bypass; X5R or X7R recommended

notes: Each address pin is set by a pull-up resistor to AVDD, a pull-down resistor to ground, or a switch to AVDD.
C7, C8 and R1 take the recommended external-component values.
The third Hall sensor should read C.
Ground pins of the controller, regulator, buck regulator and Hall sensors are outside this circuit.

circuits.title: Brushed-DC motor and solenoid drive, DRV8311H
circuits.description: The hardware variant runs a brushed DC motor across OUTA and OUTB as a full H-bridge, so it can turn either way, and drives a solenoid load from OUTC to VM with the third half-bridge. The controller supplies all six PWM inputs; MODE, SLEW and GAIN are each set by a tie to AVDD or AGND, a 47 kΩ resistor to AGND, or an open pin. Power, current sensing, CSAREF and nFAULT connect as in the BLDC circuits.

parts.note: CAVDD; X5R or X7R, 6.3 V recommended
CSAREF bypass; X5R or X7R recommended

operation.text: DRV8311H is configured by three four-level pins and accepts 6x or 3x PWM. DRV8311S is configured over SPI and adds PWM generation mode, settable retry times, dead time, delay compensation and fault reporting registers; it has no nSLEEP pin. DRV8311P uses tSPI, has nSLEEP, PWM_SYNC and two address pins, and works only in PWM generation mode. The H and S parts share a pinout apart from the four configuration or SPI pins.
Three half-bridges of N-channel MOSFETs. A doubler charge pump makes the high-side gate voltage and allows 100 % duty; an internal regulator from VM supplies the low-side gate drive.

Each phase has its own high and low inputs: INHx high alone turns the high side on, INLx high alone turns the low side on, and both low or both high leave the output Hi-Z. Selected by MODE tied to AGND or 47 kΩ to AGND (H), or PWM_MODE = 00b or 01b (S).

INHx sets the phase high or low and INLx low forces it Hi-Z. Where Hi-Z is never needed, the INLx pins can be tied high, for example to AVDD. Selected by MODE open or tied to AVDD (H), or PWM_MODE = 10b (S).
The MODE pin of the H variant is latched at power-up, so change it only with nSLEEP low; on the S variant set all INHx and INLx low before writing PWM_MODE. Changes during tWAKE are to be avoided.

The S and P variants can make the PWM themselves: a 12-bit counter set by PWM_PRD_OUT runs up/down, up, or down (PWMCNTR_MODE), and each phase's high side is on while its PWM_DUTY_OUTx exceeds the counter, provided PWM_EN is 1. A duty value above the period gives 100 %. Dead time from TDEAD_CTRL is inserted at both edges. PWM_STATE chooses per phase whether the high side, low side or both follow the PWM, which permits continuous or discontinuous switching. On the S variant, PWM_SYNC enters on INLB and the other INx pins are ignored. Trapezoidal, sinusoidal and FOC control all work in this mode.

PWM_OSC_SYNC selects how the driver's roughly 20 MHz clock is tied to the controller: 1h measures the PWM_SYNC period into PWM_SYNC_PRD so the controller can correct the period; 2h restarts the counter on each PWM_SYNC rising edge, ignoring PWMG_PERIOD; 5h trims the oscillator to 20 MHz from a 20 kHz PWM_SYNC (1000 clocks per period ideally); 6h does both the trim and the restart, again at 20 kHz only; 7h trims the oscillator from SCLK, using the clock frequency in SPICLK_FREQ_SYNC and a count of cycles in SPISYNC_ACRCY, which sets the resulting accuracy.
On the H variant GAIN, SLEW and MODE each read one of four levels: tied to AGND, 47 kΩ ±5% to AGND, open, or tied to AVDD. Faults show on nFAULT only, without detailed diagnostics.

A 3.3 V linear regulator, 3.3 V nominal at no load, powers the internal logic and up to 100 mA of outside circuits such as a small controller. Its input VIN_AVDD may equal VM or be a separate supply above or below it. Bypass AVDD with an X5R or X7R ceramic of up to 4.7 µF, 6.3 V, returned straight to the neighbouring AGND pin.
Needs one capacitor from CP to VM and stops while nSLEEP is low.

Gate drive current sets the output edge rate, measured between 20 % and 80 % of VM; four settings via the SLEW pin or SLEW_RATE bits. The edge rate governs radiated emission, diode recovery spikes and switching transients.

Shoot-through is prevented by watching each MOSFET's gate-source voltage and turning one side on only after the other has fallen below its turn-off level (handshake). TDEAD_CTRL can add 200 ns to 1.4 µs on the SPI variants. When the controller inserts its own dead time, the driver uses whichever is longer.

Measured from an input edge to the change at OUTx; it covers the input deglitch, a small digital delay and the analog driver, and grows as the slew setting slows. Delay and dead time are given as typical and maximum only: depending on the current direction during synchronous switching they can come out shorter than typical, and they can be longer when the internal turn-on is slowed to avoid dV/dt coupling.
With DLYCMP_EN = 1 the driver adds a variable delay so that edges with current into and out of OUTx both reach a target of tPD + tDEAD, reducing duty-cycle distortion.

INHx, INLx, nSLEEP, SCLK and SDI have internal pulldowns; keep them low in sleep to avoid leakage through those resistors. nSCS has an internal pullup to AVDD. nFAULT is open drain and needs a pullup; SDO is push-pull with a Hi-Z state.

Each low-side FET has a sense FET whose current is converted to a voltage on SOx, centred on VREF/2 where VREF is the CSAREF voltage, with gain 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 2 V/A (GAIN pin or CSA_GAIN). Output stays linear from 0.25 V to VREF − 0.25 V. No shunt resistor is needed.

A ground difference between the sense FET and power FET gives an offset that depends on current. It does not matter for trapezoidal or single-shunt-style control, but in sensorless sinusoidal or FOC control with two or three amplifiers it adds distortion unless the correction equations are applied in firmware.

SOx is normally sampled by the controller's ADC. A low-pass RC near the ADC with a cutoff at least 10 times the PWM frequency for trapezoidal and 100 times for sinusoidal commutation removes noise; 330 Ω with 22 pF adds little capacitance and keeps the settling time.
Below the VM UVLO threshold the FETs, charge pump and logic all stop; they resume when VM recovers. The NPOR status is latched until cleared by CLR_FLT or an nSLEEP reset pulse.

VIN_AVDD, AVDD and CP undervoltage are always enabled; each turns the FETs off and pulls nFAULT low, and VIN_AVDD or AVDD undervoltage also stops SPI. Recovery is automatic once the supply returns and tRETRY passes (slow or fast per UVP_MODE on SPI parts, fast 5 ms on the H part). CSAREF undervoltage is off by default (CSAREFUV_EN enables it on SPI parts, always off on the H part); when on it disables the amplifiers. FAULT and UVP stay latched until cleared.

Current above IOCP for longer than the deglitch time is an OCP event; a blanking time after each PWM edge ignores ringing. The H variant uses 9 A or 5 A by MODE, 1 µs deglitch, 0.2 µs blanking and 5 ms automatic retry. SPI parts choose level, deglitch, blanking and mode: automatic retry with slow or fast time, latched shutdown cleared by CLR_FLT or nSLEEP pulse, report only on nFAULT, or disabled. FAULT and OCP flags stay set until cleared.
Above TOTW the OT and OTW flags set; nFAULT reports it only when OTW_EN = 1 (off on the H part). Operation continues.

Above the shutdown limit all FETs and the charge pump turn off and nFAULT goes low; operation restarts after the die cools and tRETRY passes (fixed fast 5 ms on the H part, slow or fast by OTSD_MODE on SPI parts). Cannot be disabled.

nSLEEP low puts the device in sleep after tSLEEP: FETs, amplifiers, charge pump, AVDD regulator and SPI all off. nSLEEP high with VM above UVLO starts operation after tWAKE. nFAULT is held low while the regulators start or stop, for no longer than tWAKE or tSLEEP.

Latched faults clear by the CLR_FLT bit or by a high-low-high pulse on nSLEEP whose low time falls within tRST; a longer low starts a full shutdown. The pulse does not disturb the regulators or settings.

SPI frames are 24 bits: R/W, a 6-bit address, header parity, then 16 data bits including a data parity bit. SDO returns 8 status bits then 16 data bits. Data is sampled on the falling SCLK edge and launched on the rising edge, MSB first; SCLK must be low at both nSCS edges, and frames are multiples of 16 clocks (minimum 16), otherwise a frame error is flagged.

tSPI frames carry a 16-bit header: R/W, a 4-bit device ID (top two bits 00, lower two from AD1 and AD0), an 8-bit address, two zero bits and parity. Valid IDs are 0 to 3 plus 15, a general call that every device accepts for writes. Separate read and write address pointers auto-increment, so one transaction can write one set of registers while reading another after a header-only read-address frame. Multiple devices share nSCS, SCLK, SDI and SDO.

Even parity over each 16-bit block, enabled by SPI_PEN (off at reset, enabling it is recommended). A parity error is latched, shown on nFAULT and in SPI_PARITY, and blocks the write; a frame error sets FRM_ERR.

Local bulk capacitance on VM keeps the supply steady against motor current steps and returned energy; how much depends on peak current, supply capability and wiring inductance, allowed ripple, motor type and braking method. Rate bulk capacitors above the operating voltage.

Place the bulk capacitor to keep the high-current loop short, with wide traces and many vias. Put the small ceramic capacitors right at AVDD, CP, CSAREF, VIN_AVDD and VM. Use wide traces for outputs. Keep PGND and AGND as separate regions joined by a net tie, with non-power circuitry and the thermal pad on AGND, or use one plane with the switching outputs kept away from analog and digital signals. Solder the pad to a top-layer ground plane with many vias to a large bottom plane, and add as much connected copper as possible for heat.

Losses are standby, LDO, FET conduction and switching, and dead-time diode conduction; conduction dominates. RDS(on) rises with temperature, and start-up and fault currents must be included. Thermal shutdown acting is a sign of too much dissipation, too little heat sinking or too high an ambient.
